summary: Shogo Watanabe specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. After studying at Toyo University, he served there from around 1990 to 2024, becoming a professor in roughly 2003. He later held posts at Taisho University and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Shohaku Okumura is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Komazawa University (~1968–1972) and under Kōshō Uchiyama (1970–1975). He founded Sanshin Zen Community and served as director of the Sōtō Zen Buddhism International Center (1997–2010).
Shoichi Ozawa worked in Japanology and history and archaeology. He studied at Waseda University from around 1950 to 1954 and held a post at the Open University of Japan.

Shoji Mori specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Toyo University (~1962–1971) under Giyu Nishi. He worked at the Okurayama Institute (~1971) before serving as assistant professor (~1978–1988) and professor (~1988–2009) at Toyo University.
Shoju Inaba was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He taught at Nagoya University as a part-time lecturer and served as a professor at Otani University from around 1957 to 1980.
Shojun Bando worked in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1952 to 1959. He later held posts at Ueno Gakuen University (~1968–1980) and Otani University (~1980–1998).

Shokin Furuta specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying at the University of Tokyo, Tokyo University of Education, and under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki. He served as professor at Hokkaido University (~1953–1968) and Nihon University (~1968–1982).
Shoko Kanaoka worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He served on the faculty at Toyo University, where he held a professorship attested in 1987 and a post attested in 2000.

Shoko Miyabayashi specialized in Buddhist studies. He completed undergraduate and master's studies at Taisho University (1948–1955), where he went on to serve as lecturer (1960), assistant professor (1962), and Dean of Buddhist Studies (1978–2002).

Shoko Miyata works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Miyata has served as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, both attested in 2026.
Shoko Takeuchi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and later served there as professor emeritus (attested 1987–1995).

Shoko Watanabe studied Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University under Ernst Leumann and Naoshiro Tsuji. His posts included Taisho University (1935–1943), Kyushu University (1948–1953), and Toyo University (1956–1969).

Shoku Bando specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. After studying at Kyoto University of Education, Otani University, and the University of Freiburg, he held posts attested in 1987 at the Abhidharma Research Institute, Kyoto University, and Fukui Prefectural College.

Shoryu Katsura works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Toronto under A. K. Warder, among others, and held faculty posts at Hiroshima University (1976–2004) and Ryukoku University (2004–2015).

Shoshin Fukihara specialized in Buddhist studies, studying at Otani University and Horyu-ji under Join Saeki and Susumu Yamaguchi. His academic career included posts at Shinshu College, Doho University (~1950–1965), and Otani University (~1947–1975).

Shoshin Kuwayama is a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Kyoto University (~1958–1966), he served there from around 1966 to 2002, notably at the Institute for Research in Humanities.

Shoshun Hayashidera specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Hayashidera held a post at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2011) and serves as a professor at Hokkaido University (attested 2026).

Shoson Miyamoto was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University, the University of Tokyo, and the University of Oxford. His main professorships were at Toyo, Tokyo, Waseda, and Komazawa universities.

Shou-chien Shih is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He served as a professor at National Taiwan University from around 1984 to 1997 and was director of the National Palace Museum from roughly 2000 to 2004.

Shoyu Hanayama specialized in Buddhist studies and studied at the University of Tokyo (~1950–1960). He served as vice president at Musashino University (~1966–1995) and chairperson at Bukkyo D伝do Kyokai (~1985–1995).
